title: The names of Yama

words.meaning: to the son of Vivasvat (the Sun)
to the destroyer of all beings
to the one who stands highest

words.role: marks the end of the formula

samasa.vigraha: वृकस्य उदरम् इव उदरं यस्य सः
samasa.meaning: whose belly is like a wolf’s

translation.literal: To Yama, the King of Dharma, to Death and to the Ender, to the son of Vivasvat, to Time, and to the destroyer of all beings; to Audumbara, to Dadhna, to the dark one, to the highest, to the wolf-bellied, to Citra, to Citragupta indeed, homage. “To Citragupta indeed homage — om, homage.”
translation.readable: Homage to Yama — King of Dharma, Death, the Ender, son of the Sun, Time, destroyer of all beings; to Audumbara, Dadhna, the dark one, the highest, the wolf-bellied, Citra and Citragupta. To Citragupta, homage; om, homage.

sandhi_exceptions.note: at the break between the two halves of the verse, where the recitation pauses; the witness leaves the vowels unjoined

lines: यमाय धर्मराजाय मृत्यवे चान्तकाय च वैवस्वताय कालाय सर्वभूतक्षयाय च औदुम्बराय दध्नाय नीलाय परमेष्ठिने वृकोदराय चित्राय चित्रगुप्ताय वै नमः
चित्रगुप्ताय वै नम ओं नम इति
units.pause_note: The two verses end at चित्रगुप्ताय वै नमः; the refrain चित्रगुप्ताय वै नम ओं नम इति follows after a pause (S writes no danda between them).

meaning: Fourteen names of Yama, the god of death and of dharma, said facing south, his direction. Several are transparent — Dharmarāja, Mṛtyu (Death), Antaka (the Ender), Vaivasvata (son of the Sun), Kāla (Time) — while others (Audumbara, Dadhna) are traditional names whose sense is not obvious; the list ends with Citragupta, who keeps the record of deeds. The last words are repeated with om namaḥ iti.
in_the_rite: Step yama-vandana, all three services, facing south.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Two anuṣṭubh (śloka) verses with a refrain. The vowels of च औदुम्बराय stand unjoined at the break between the verses. M reads धर्मर्राजाय (corrections.json).

flags.text: S writes the verses and the refrain with no danda between them, so नमः चित्रगुप्ताय (verse end, refrain start) stands unjoined inside one line. The padaccheda is two lines (verses | refrain): a danda is needed after the first चित्रगुप्ताय वै नमः (it changes no letter).
